The tip rejects them with 'has been created in a concurrent state'. conc3_selected_at_inner_depth: Java exit 200, stderr 'ERROR / 1 / Syntax Error? (Assumed diagram type: sequence)', and the tip renders it.

java_trace.counter: CucaDiagram.cpt2 is one AtomicInteger per diagram (CucaDiagram.java:128), not per composite or depth. startingPass sets it back to 1 before each of the three passes StateDiagram.getRequiredPass declares (CucaDiagram.java:159-165, StateDiagram.java:66-68, PSystemCommandFactory.java:93-107). getUniqueSequence2 is addAndGet(1), so the first separator of every pass is CONC2 (CucaDiagram.java:816-818).
java_trace.advance_on_reuse: concurrentState calls getUniqueSequence2 before quarkInContext, unconditionally (StateDiagram.java:201-204). The counter advances on every separator, whether the name then reuses a quark or creates one.
java_trace.name_count: quarkInContextSafe reuses a quark only when Plasma.countByName(name) == 1 and that quark is not the current group (CucaDiagram.java:264-272). Plasma.register counts every quark that Quark.child creates, data or not (Plasma.java:63-72, Quark.java:116-140). The separator's own CONCn group is such a quark. Quarks persist across passes; only the counter and the group stack are reset.
java_trace.declaration_after_separator: conc2_declared_after_separator, pass one: the separator in House creates House.CONC2 (count 0). 'state CONC2' then sees count 1, and that quark is the current group, so it creates House.CONC2.CONC2. Pass two: the separator is CONC2 again, count is now 2, so it resolves to House.child(CONC2) = House.CONC2, the existing region. 'state CONC2' resolves to House.CONC2.CONC2, whose parent is the current group, so checkConcurrentStateOk passes. The root link '[*] --> CONC2' sees count 2 and creates a root leaf CONC2. conc3_after_two_separators is the same with CONC3: concurrentState first pops the CONC2 group (StateDiagram.java:197-198), so the current quark is House, not the earlier region.
java_trace.group_type: gotoGroup calls muteToGroupType on every entry (CucaDiagram.java:350-356). 'state X {' mutes X to STATE, and a separator that reuses X mutes it to CONCURRENT_STATE. checkConcurrentStateOkInternal reads the type at the time of the command (StateDiagram.java:75-90).
java_trace.final_error: conc3_selected_at_inner_depth: every command passes. The pass-two separator in Inner reuses Outer.CONC2.Inner.CONC3 and mutes it to CONCURRENT_STATE. The root link to CONC3 passes, because CONC3's direct parent Inner is a STATE. StateDiagram.checkFinalError (StateDiagram.java:232-266) then walks all ancestors: CONC3's nearest concurrent ancestor is Outer.CONC2, and [*]'s is none, so it returns an error. finalizeDiagram locates it at it.next() of the rewound iterator, which is line 1 (PSystemCommandFactory.java:115-121). The trace holds two lines, so PSystemError.score is 20 (PSystemError.java:379-382). SequenceDiagramFactory runs first (PSystemBuilder.java:131-135) and fails at 'state Outer {' with 'Syntax Error?' and the same score of 20. mergeV2 keeps the first maximum (PSystemErrorUtils.java:85-92), so Java reports sequence's line-1 'Syntax Error?'.

rust_divergence: parse/state.rs counts only State entries when it looks up a short name. Synthetic region ids live in region_ids, so they are invisible to that count. The pass-two separator therefore sees one CONC2 (or CONC3) state and reuses the leaf declared inside the region as the region itself. advance_concurrent_region also compares the sole quark with the previous region, not the owner that concurrentState pops back to. The state parser has no checkFinalError. Separately, resolve_state_id_in picks a sole 'compatible' quark when the count is 2 or more, which Java never does. And region_ids is a set that only grows, so a later 'state X {' never mutes a reused quark back to STATE.
planned_change: State parser only. (1) Count a short name over State ids together with synthetic region ids, with no duplicates. (2) The separator compares the sole quark with the owning composite, not the previous region. (3) Resolution: count == 1 and the quark is not the current group means that quark, then checkConcurrentStateOk. Otherwise the child of the current scope. Drop the compatibility filter. (4) Track each quark's current group type. A composite open mutes it to STATE, and a separator mutes the region to CONCURRENT_STATE. checkConcurrentStateOk reads that type. (5) After the pass, port checkFinalError over the transitions with the nearest-concurrent-ancestor walk. When it fails, report 'Syntax Error?' at the first content line, which is the sequence factory's tie-winning error when line 1 is a state command. No name-keyed logic, no renderer edit unless a measured case needs one.
residue_declared_in_advance: Rust models Java passes one and two. Pass three re-runs declarations and separators. It differs only when a pass-two link adds a second quark with a separator's sequence name, and that is not modelled.

The final error copies the sequence factory's line 1. When the sequence, class, activity or description grammar accepts the leading lines, Java reports that factory's later error instead. Rust does not run the other factories.

A short name whose only quark is a synthetic region (a link or declaration of CONCn from outside) resolves to that region in Java. The renderer has no State for a synthetic region. This is probed in the held-out batch, not fitted.
